newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: UNICEF says Afghan truce holds.
newsitem.headline: UNICEF says Afghan truce holds.

text.p: The U.N. children's fund, UNICEF, said on Monday a five-day truce between Afghanistan's warring factions to help a mass polio vaccination campaign was holding, although a private news service reported new fighting.
The truce, due to last from April 6-10, was negotiated by UNICEF and the World Health Organisation (WHO) with the Taleban Islamic militia and northern Uzbek chief General Abdul Rashid Dostum.
The truce "is reported by UNICEF field offices to be holding throughout Afghanistan", a UNICEF statement in Islamabad said.

But a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said the Taleban launched a new offensive on Monday morning against Dostum's forces in the northwestern province of Badghis, advancing at least five km (three miles) in the Bala Murghab area.
Dostum's jet fighters carried out heavy bombing of Taleban positions, the Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said, quoting a Taleban spokesman in the southern city of Kandahar.
There was no independent confirmation of the report, which said six of Dostum's and three Taleban troops were killed.
There was also no immediate comment from the Taleban administration in the Afghan capital Kabul.
UNICEF said it launched the first of the planned two rounds of the polio immunisation campaign with the WHO and the Afghan Ministry of Public Health on Sunday.
It said it hoped that 3.8 million children under five years old would be given oral polio drops during the first round.
"Severe winter weather permitting, every district wil be covered for the first time", the statement said.
The vaccination campaign marks another step in a polio eradication initiative in the countries of the Middle East, the Caucasus and central Asia, UNICEF said.

The campaign was opened by Taleban Public Health Minister, Mullah Abbas Akhund, in Kabul and head of political affairs in Dostum's administration, Nooruddin Hamsangar, in the northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif.
Afghanistan, devastated by more than 17 years of civil war, has had much of its health infrastructure destroyed.
UNICEF is supporting the campaign through the provision of polio vaccine, as well as equipment for the storage and transportation of vaccines to all vaccination posts, the statement said.
It said more than 13,000 volunteers, vaccinators and other health workers had been trained and mobilised for immunisation days.
The Dutch, Swedish and British governments as well as the European Community Humanitarian Office, the Centre for Disease Control in Atlanta and Rotary International have provided funds.
